Paramedics bring a 30-year-old male to the emergency department with altered consciousness after
finding him unresponsive at a bus stop. Upon evaluation, he exhibits slurred speech and drowsiness.
His vital signs show: temperature 98.1°F (36.7°C), blood pressure 151/78 mmHg, heart rate 80/min,
respiratory rate 19/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air. The physical examination reveals a
drowsy patient with miotic pupils who is easily aroused by voice and sternal rub but quickly falls back
asleep. Bowel sounds are diminished. He can state his name and is oriented to location, with an
otherwise normal neurological examination. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
Answer Choices: (A) Flumazenil (B) CT head without contrast (C) Physostigmine administration (D)
Naloxone (E) N-acetylcysteine therapy (F) Glucagon administration (G) Sodium bicarbonate infusion
(H) Observation (I) Activated charcoal (J) Immediate intubation
 A. Activated charcoal
B. Observation
C. CT head without contrast
D. Flumazenil
E. Naloxone
F. Glucagon administration
G. Immediate intubation
H. Physostigmine administration
I. N-acetylcysteine therapy
J. Sodium bicarbonate infusion
